title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.43): Σ is a conformal 2-sphere with a 3-element subset J = {R_i}. The symmetric group S_J acts by direct conformal automorphisms. The full conformal automorphism group of (Σ,J) is S_J × {1,τ}, where τ is the anti-holomorphic involution fixing the R_i. There is a unique S_J-invariant round metric up to scale, which identifies Σ with the unit sphere of a 3-dimensional Euclidean space E_J. V ⊂ E is the plane spanned by the R_j, and Σ_R = Σ ∩ V is the 'real circle'. Three 2-element torsors are introduced: ϖ (orientations of Σ or E), ω (orientations of J, i.e. cyclic orders, i.e. orientations of Σ_R) and ε = π_0(Σ∖Σ_R) (the two hemispheres, equivalently π_0(E∖V)).

This page carries out the linear algebra.
(4) Invariance under the cyclic 3-rotation forces Σ_j R_j = 0: the centroid of the R_j is the centre of the sphere.
(5) Hence V is canonically isomorphic to V_J(R) = ker(sum: R^J → R), the standard (reflection) representation of S_J. Explicitly, R_j corresponds to the image of the basis vector e_j, i.e. e_j − (1/3)Σe.
(6) Using the third formula of (3), the orthogonal line Δ = V^⊥ (the 'polar axis') is canonically isometric to R(ε). This is the real line twisted by the hemisphere torsor ε: a unit normal vector is the same as a choice of hemisphere.
(7) Hence E ≅ V_J(R) ⊕ R(ε) as Euclidean spaces. The metric on V_J(R) is the unique quadratic form q with q(R_j) = 1. In the basis (R_i, R_j), with R_k = (−1,−1), one gets q = x² − xy + y²: the conditions a = c = 1 and a + 2b + c = 1 give 2b = −1. Geometrically, the R_i form an equilateral triangle inscribed in the unit circle of V. A marginal note says q is S_J-invariant.
The S_J-action on E is the tautological action on V_J(R) plus the sign character on Δ.

Check of the sign: a transposition acts on the sphere as the rotation by π about the axis through the fixed point. On V this rotation is a reflection (det −1), so on Δ it must act by −1 for the total determinant to be +1. It also swaps the two hemispheres, consistent with ε being the sign torsor as an S_J-set.

Purpose: a fully canonical, torsor-explicit, symmetric model of P^1 minus three points with its S_3 × Z/2 symmetry. The next page announces this as a 'preliminary exercise in Galois synthesis': computing the fundamental groupoid of Σ* = Σ∖J with base points near the R_i (tangential base points via a compactification). This is the first building block of the Teichmüller tower in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical errors. The formula x² − xy + y² and the equilateral-triangle picture are correct, as is the sign action on Δ (needed for the action to be by rotations).
Minor point: the metric is only defined up to a scalar λ, and normalising Σ as the unit sphere is a choice of scale. The author handles this implicitly.

ideas.what: Canonical Euclidean model of (P^1, three points): E_J = V_J(R) ⊕ R(ε), with the marked points as an equilateral triangle on the equator and S_J acting by standard representation ⊕ sign
ideas.modern_name: Standard/reflection representation of S_3 and the dihedral-symmetric model of P^1 ∖ {0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (folklore; e.g. the octahedral/dihedral symmetric pictures of P^1 minus three points)
ideas.where_published: The S_3 × {1,τ} symmetry of the 'two-point/three-point' building blocks is discussed in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in general terms; this explicit linear-algebra model is not published as far as known

ideas.what: Identifying the polar axis V^⊥ with the line R(ε) twisted by the 2-torsor of hemispheres (systematic use of 2-element torsors of orientations ϖ, ω, ε)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's habitual torsor-canonical style (e.g. Récoltes et Semailles remarks, SGA), but not this specific setting

ideas.what: Program announced on the next page: the fundamental groupoid of the thrice-punctured sphere with base points near the punctures, as a warm-up for Galois synthesis and Teichmüller groupoids
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points; fundamental groupoid of P^1 ∖ {0,1,∞}; Grothendieck–Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points), Ihara, Drinfeld (1990, GT), Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine linear algebra setting up a canonical symmetric model of the thrice-punctured sphere. Its only distinctive feature is the systematic torsor bookkeeping (R(ε) for the polar axis), which is stylistic rather than a new result. The broader program is already known from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'vu la géom formule (3)' should read 'vu la 3ième formule (3)', i.e. the third line of (3), defining ε, which justifies Δ ≅ R(ε).
'ou dans V_J(R) on prend' should be 'où dans V_J(R) on prend'.
Line 'Il est clair, et je l'ai expliqué, que q est invariant...' is a left-margin insertion; the wording 'je l'ai expliqué' is uncertain.
'si on prend comme base deux R_i, R_j, R_k de coordonnées (−1,−1)' should be understood as 'si on prend comme base deux R_i, R_j, R_k ayant les coordonnées (−1,−1)'.
Final line: 'par son opération tautologique sur V(J) et l'opération par sg(g) sur Δ' (a struck-out word precedes 'tautologique').
